verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is readable: a public getsentry/sentry GitHub repo exists, the full product is self-hostable for free, and community users say seeing the code helped with advanced integrations. However, community evidence says Sentry moved to the BSL, which users treat as no longer fully open, so the 'open license' part is only partly met. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of the license terms, evidence that the license is OSI-approved or permissive, and clarity on which components remain under open licenses.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
the fully open source code helped a ton with advanced integrations, since they could see exactly what happens instead of relying only on the docs
